On your turn, take one of the two face-up cards in the center and use it to replace a face-down card in your pyramid, then place the replaced card face up in the center. When all pyramids are revealed, you can either keep your Star card for 3 bonus points or discard it to draw one last card and improve your pyramid. You score only for ascending rows: mixed colors give 1 point per card, single-color rows give 2 points per card, plus 1 point per star and 3 extra if you kept your Star card. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary IPSO There are 90 cards numbered 1 to 90 of which: 18 are magenta (those ending in 1 or 6) 18 are yellow (those ending in 2 or 7) 18 are green (those ending in 3 or 8) 18 are blue (those ending in 4 or 9) 18 are orange (those ending in 0 or 5) These cards may have a number of stars on them that give bonus points. 1 star for each card in (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85) 2 stars for each card in (16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75) Goal of the game: Build rows of ascending numbers to score the most points possible. Rules: You start with 14 face down cards forming a pyramid with a Star card at the top. Two cards are taken from the draw pile and placed face up in the centre. Choose one of the cards and place on your pyramid, swapping it with a face down card. The face down card is now flipped, replacing the selected card in the centre. A row must be in ascending order to score. Not the entire pyramid, but each row separately. Scoring For each valid row (cards are in ascending order): 1 point per card 1 additional point per card if all cards in the row are also the same color 1 point for each star in the row (remember the row must be valid for stars to count) Plus the 3 point star bonus if the star card is unused. In case of a tie, the winner is the player with the most stars on their number cards. At the end You have 2 options: You can either choose to keep your Star card and gain 3 points or You can choose to discard your Star card and take another turn. The two face up centre cards are placed on the bottom of the draw pile and a card is drawn from the draw pile. You may then use it to replace any card already placed or discard it. This may useful when only one card is non-ascendant. [Rating: 2/10] Meh, another game that takes the basic Golf mechanism and makes it worse.  Since you can't peek at any of your cards, and you are just choosing between 2 cards each turn, it's mostly luck of the draw. A little bit of hedging your bets to ensure you achieve ascending order, but I don't see the point of playing this over say Lucky Numbers.

[Rating: 2/10] A few plays on BGA. This game is way too random - there's no strategy or even thinking and you are almost entirely at the mercy of the deck. Playing it just made me angry.
